summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived biography of A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, an Indian aerospace scientist who served as the 11th President of India from 2002 to 2007. It covers his birth and death details, his career at DRDO and ISRO in missile and space programmes, his role in the 1998 Pokhran-II nuclear tests, and his election as a widely admired 'People's President'. It also lists his awards and notable work.
one_line: Biography of A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, Indian aerospace scientist and 11th President of India (2002–2007).
key_facts: Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam was the 11th President of India, serving in office from 25 July 2002 to 25 July 2007.
Abdul Kalam was born on 15 October 1931 in Rameswaram, Madras Presidency, British India.
Abdul Kalam died on 27 July 2015 in Shillong, Meghalaya, India, aged 83.
Abdul Kalam was an aerospace scientist who studied physics and aerospace engineering.
Abdul Kalam spent four decades as a scientist and science administrator, mainly at the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
Abdul Kalam was known as the Missile Man of India for his work on ballistic missile and launch vehicle technology.
Abdul Kalam played a pivotal organisational, technical, and political role in India's Pokhran-II nuclear tests in 1998.
India's first nuclear test was the original nuclear test in 1974, preceding the Pokhran-II tests.
Abdul Kalam was elected as the 11th President of India in 2002 with the support of both the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party and the then-opposition Indian National Congress.
Abdul Kalam was widely referred to as the "People's President".
After a single term, Abdul Kalam returned to civilian life of education, writing and public service.
Abdul Kalam received the Bharat Ratna in 1997, India's highest civilian honour.
Abdul Kalam received the Hoover Medal in 2009 and the NSS Von Braun Award in 2013.
Abdul Kalam's notable work includes the book Wings of Fire.
Abdul Kalam's alma maters were St. Joseph's College, Tiruchirappalli and Madras Institute of Technology.
